data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network is more resilient to correlated failure because it shifts the failure mode from 'systemic collapse' to 'partial degradation' by eliminating the unified control plane as a single point of failure.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services share a critical common dependency (e.g., a single DNS provider or cloud region).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The cost of managing diversity exceeds the benefit, leading to poor maintenance and higher individual failure rates.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Operational diversity (different OS, languages, and deployment pipelines) prevents a single 'poison pill' update or zero-day exploit from propagating across the entire network, whereas a large service's internal redundancy is often undermined by a shared orchestration layer that distributes the same failure to all redundant nodes.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
